_comment: Declared deviations and withdrawals: differences and absences that are known,
explained and expected. Read conformance/deviations.py for why this exists.
Every entry MUST name: kind ('deviation' or 'withdrawal'), scope (cases, and for
deviations ports/stages/optionally paths), reason, basis (user decision or bus
frame), declared date, owner, and removed_when - the EVENT that retires it.
kind 'deviation': the case IS run and a difference against the golden is expected.
kind 'withdrawal': the sample was taken out, the case is NOT run - there is nothing
to diff, and the report must show it as NOT verified, never as verified-with-a-
difference. A withdrawal must name specific cases, never '*'.
A date is not an exit condition; an entry without removed_when is a permanent
loosening in disguise. An entry that matches nothing where it applies is STALE.

deviations.reason: The ports carry the passport page registration (page_registration/: template locator, quad fit, line refinement, line dewarp) and reproduce the canvas of both internal-passport cases exactly (borders.canvas and deskew.canvas match). What does not converge bitwise is the line refinement. Its line evidence is the same since 2026-10-08: both ports call the reference's cv::createLineSegmentDetector (.NET through OpenCvSharp's LineSegmentDetector, which the first port had missed; Go through a small C++ shim, gocv 0.43 does not bind it), raw segments equal to the reference's; until then they used Canny+HoughLinesP. What remains is the 4-parameter IRLS fit on a hand-written Levenberg-Marquardt instead of scipy.optimize.least_squares (trf) and a RANSAC that does not draw NumPy's PCG64 samples - with LSD in place the Go port runs INTPASSPORT_1997 clean and keeps 4 differences on 2011, .NET 442 differences against 446 before. A slightly different refinement homography moves the field boxes by 1-7 px on Go (median 1, p90 3) and 1-10 px on .NET, shifts detector confidences by up to 0.03, and on each case flips one character of one field where the crop edge crosses a glyph (Birth_date '03.ABTYCT' vs '03.ABRYCT' on 1997; Birth_place_ru 'С.' vs 'С' on 2011 for .NET). Measured 2026-09-21 on the models-v6 goldens; both ports are deterministic run to run (RANSAC seeded). D-01 (MRZ re-read ladder) retired the same day: all three ports carry the ladder now and the entry matched nothing. In this tree both passport cases are withdrawn (W-01, W-04), so this entry records the ports' state and matches nothing here until a synthetic replacement returns the cases.
deviations.basis: user decision of 2026-09-19 (release 4.5.0 in one window with the ports; a residual that cannot be made pixel-exact is declared with its measured size rather than left to hold the release); measured on the ports' conformance reports of 2026-09-21
deviations.removed_when: the ports' line-refinement fit reproduces scipy's least_squares and the quad-fit RANSAC draws the reference's samples (or the reference switches to a fit the ports can reproduce bitwise) - then this entry goes stale and must be deleted

deviations.reason: On this case with models-v7 the template locates page 2 only; page 3 is cut straight from its Borders quad ('borders-spare') in the reference and in the Kotlin port alike. Everything before that cut matches (sources, page-2 registration method and 26 inliers, native scale 0.4954, page-2 line refinement to the 5th decimal, the same dewarp decision). The spare page itself does not: the line refinement finds 30 LSD segments on it against 31 in the reference - a different input picture, since LSD is the same binding on both sides - so its refinement homography and its dewarp decision differ, and field boxes move by 1-4 px (38 values in fields.bbox, 19 in words, 45 in the view model; the recognised text is identical). Narrowed to the spare page's cut, not pinned: the likeliest source is quad_fit's RANSAC, which draws with Kotlin's own PRNG instead of NumPy's PCG64 (QuadFit.kt says so and names this as the place to revisit); warp interpolation is the other candidate. Measured 2026-09-26/27 by a traced run against the reference. The sample is withdrawn from this tree (W-01); the entry applies where the case runs.
deviations.basis: user decision 2026-09-26 (release 4.6.0 with weight set models-v7); the 4.5.0 rule that a residual which cannot be made pixel-exact is declared with its measured size rather than left to hold the release (decision of 2026-09-19)
deviations.removed_when: quad_fit's RANSAC in the Kotlin port draws the same samples as the reference (a PCG64 port), or the spare-page cut is otherwise shown to match - then this case runs clean and the entry goes stale and must be deleted

deviations.reason: Not a port defect: the REFERENCE itself decides this card differently on another platform. The card's canvas is rebuilt from its printed blank only when the Borders canvas is skewed by >= 1 % (Pipeline.CARD_SKEW_KEEP); this card measures 0.0076 on the Windows wheel the goldens were written with, so the reference keeps the Borders canvas. The skew comes from a MAGSAC homography over SIFT matches, and SIFT with nfeatures=6000 cuts its points with std::nth_element, whose order depends on the C++ library OpenCV was built with. The reference Python run on Linux (opencv-python-headless 4.12 in the .NET port's container) gives the ports' numbers to the last digit: 1760 coarse matches against 1670, skew 0.0118, the card re-cut from the template, canvas 1414x1013 against 1387x963. The same reference on the same Windows machine with cv2.setUseOptimized(False) flips too (1353 inliers against 1038, skew 0.0112). Every port then reads a different canvas and everything after borders.segments differs. With the threshold moved to match the reference's decision the Kotlin port runs all 43 stages clean, so the kept-Borders branch, the fields and the reading are exact. Measured 2026-10-08.
deviations.basis: decision of 2026-10-07 that the ports release together with Python and are released only with conformance CLEAN or DECLARED; the 2026-09-19 rule that a residual which cannot be made exact is declared with its measured size
deviations.removed_when: the card's template match gives the same decision on every platform (a platform-independent keypoint cut in the reference, e.g. nfeatures=0 plus a stable sort, with goldens regenerated), or the goldens are written on the platform the ports are checked on - then this case runs clean and the entry goes stale and must be deleted

deviations.reason: The same platform dependence as D-07, at a size that does not change any decision: the template homography of this card differs in the 10th digit (H[0][0] 0.7994596886 on Linux against 0.7994596890 in the Windows goldens; the reference Python on Linux gives the ports' value), the card corner moves by about 0.04 px, and one edge of one field box rounds the other way (fields.bbox[9] y2 846 against 845, and the same box in the view model). 284 matches on both sides; the recognised text and the leasing stage are identical. Measured 2026-10-08.
deviations.removed_when: as D-07: the template match is made platform-independent in the reference or the goldens are written where the ports are checked - then this case runs clean and the entry goes stale and must be deleted
